answer: Because the ember liability is logged in the mirror ledger at admission, the atlas audit shows the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 40% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must thus place its own capital behind each alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. A farm of 187 pays that 55 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
